title: A world clock from one reading

blocks.text: A status page shows the current time in several offices. `WorldClock` is built with the `Clock` it must read (tests pass a fixed or a moving clock; nothing reads the system clock directly).

Write `WorldClock.show(List<ZoneId> zones)`. It returns one line per zone, in the order given: the zone ID, a space, then the time in that zone as the short English weekday, the 24-hour time and the zone's short name.

All the lines describe **one moment**. A clock keeps moving while the lines are built, so the lines must all come from **a single reading** of the clock, taken **when `show` is called**: a later call shows a later moment. The weekday and zone name are **English whatever the server's default locale** is.

cases.says: One instant shows as each zone's weekday, time and short zone name, in the order the zones were asked for.
With a clock that moves a minute each time it is read, every line still shows the same minute.
A second call on a moving clock shows the later minute, not the one read at construction.
On a server whose default locale is German, the weekday is still the English Fri.

concepts: Times in several zones are shown by reading one instant and converting it to each zone.
